I tried to comment as a reply to Unidan and as a top level comment but I'm not sure either went through... anyway: What Unidan is saying is not correct. Gasses will not unmix, as that blatantly goes against entropy. Gravity will cause some density gradients but it will not be anywhere close to the stratified layers that Unidan describes. This is because the forces driving Brownian motion and diffusion will not be overpowered by gravity.

It is still possible that areas of higher concentrations of certain gasses will form. For example, carbon dioxide traps (areas of high CO2) can form when it is produced faster that it diffuses away. For example, this can occur when an organic compound is decomposing. Source: http://www.researchgate.net/profile/Giovanni_Badino/publication/228475055_The_legend_of_carbon_dioxide_heaviness/links/00b49523a9aa33101e000000.pdf
